## Evidence (live, 2026-07-25, 2,022-item workspace)

```
$ pm next --json | jq -c '.recommended | {id,type,title}'
{"id":"pm-w7ccmv","type":"Milestone","title":"Outcome milestone: provable history ..."}

$ pm list --parent pm-w7ccmv --status all --json | jq .count
0

$ pm next --json | jq -r '.ready[] | "\(.id) \(.type)"' | head -5
pm-e02lgu Task
pm-kb5h  Chore
pm-5t33or Feature
pm-ed28wi Issue
pm-9rgaal Milestone      <-- second gate in the ready slice
```

The single recommendation an agent is told to work next is an outcome milestone with zero children. Outcome milestones are **gates**: they close when the epics beneath them meet their acceptance criteria, they never carry direct execution, and by construction they have no children to walk into. An agent that follows `pm next`, claims the recommendation, and looks for something to do finds nothing — then either releases it as a no-op or, worse, invents work under a gate.

## Two halves, one root

**Half 1 — gate classes are not held out of the actionable set.** The precedent already exists and shipped: Decision-type items are non-executable by an agent lane, so `pm next` routes them to a dedicated `decision_needed` bucket (6 items today) instead of `recommended`/`ready` (pm-eqk0). Milestone gates are the same class of thing and get no such treatment. The fix is not a Milestone special case — it is a declared, schema-driven answer to "can an agent lane execute an item of this type/shape", so extension-contributed and custom types inherit it instead of each needing a patch.

**Half 2 — `summary.containers` counts a bucket the envelope never emits.** `pm next --json` reports `summary.containers: 27`, but the envelope keys are `blocked, decision_needed, filters, held_by_others, now, output_default, ready, recommended, summary, truncation` — there is no `containers` key. An agent can see that 27 items were classified as containers and has no way to ask which. Every other classification bucket in this envelope has a worklist; this one is a dead number, which is the same defect shape as the `activity.activity` decoy key (pm-p3x4).

## Why it matters beyond one bad recommendation

`pm next` is the entry point of the agent loop and the intended input to fleet allocation (pm-3oqjnc). A recommender that hands out non-executable gates wastes an entire agent turn per occurrence, and at fleet scale it distributes the same wasted turn across many agents simultaneously. The strategic-reachability work (pm-bzmeaa) deliberately makes every active item reach an outcome milestone through typed edges — which means gates sit near the top of exactly the paths a relevance-ranked recommender favours, so this gets worse as the graph gets healthier, not better.

## Fix direction

Extend the shared actionability definition (`src/sdk/actionability.ts`, shipped by pm-uxkf/PR#579) with a declared executability dimension alongside the existing blocked-vs-ready dimension, so `next`, `context`, `list-blocked`, and `claim --next` all inherit one answer; surface the held-out sets as real envelope keys with worklists; and keep them reachable through an explicit opt-in flag so no capability is removed.
pm next recommends outcome-milestone gates as actionable work, and summary.containers counts a bucket the envelope never emits

The single pm next recommendation is currently pm-w7ccmv, an outcome milestone with zero children that no agent lane can execute, and Milestones also appear in ready[]; separately summary.containers reports 27 with no corresponding envelope key. Both are the same root: item executability is not a declared dimension of the shared actionability definition, unlike the shipped decision_needed precedent.

Item executability is a declared, schema-driven dimension of the shared actionability definition rather than a per-type special case, so custom and extension-contributed types inherit it; gate-shaped items (outcome milestones and any type declared non-executable) never appear as pm next recommended or in ready[], and are surfaced in their own envelope bucket with a worklist exactly as decision_needed already is; summary.containers either gains a matching envelope key with rows or is removed, so no summary counter names a bucket that cannot be read; the held-out sets remain reachable through an explicit opt-in flag so no capability is lost; next, context, list-blocked and claim --next all consume the one definition and agree; a spec asserts that a workspace whose only unblocked items are gates returns no recommendation with an explanatory reason rather than recommending a gate

message: Strategic reachability edge: mirror the hierarchy rung into the typed layer so every active item resolves to an outcome milestone through an explainable implements path (pm-bzmeaa invariant), which the parent chain alone cannot express because it terminates at the roadmap root rather than at an outcome

value.text: Context-side instance 2026-07-26: the gate-recommendation defect is not confined to pm next. On this workspace pm context --limit 2 returns pm-doxj, the roadmap-root Milestone, and pm-j82fd3, an outcome-milestone gate, as both of its low_level rows — that is, the two most actionable detail rows an agent is shown are the two least executable items in the tracker. Whatever lifecycle-role or container predicate resolves the pm next half must be shared with context assembly rather than applied at one call site.
